narrative:
The system estimated an 82.3% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, it judged failure to be much more likely than success, and that estimated risk is why your law school application was denied.

The strongest reason was your third-year class standing. You were in the second decile, well below the average accepted student, who was around the sixth decile. That was the largest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year standing was the second most important factor and showed a similar pattern: also second decile and well below accepted students, reinforcing the concern. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor. At 2.90 it was below the accepted-student average of 3.23, but its influence was the only one among the top three that pointed toward passing rather than failing, so it slightly softened rather than drove the rejection.

To move forward, ask admissions for a human review and explain any contextual factors behind your early grades. Focus on raising your academic standing, consider additional coursework or credentials that demonstrate readiness, and speak with an advisor about a realistic bar-exam preparation plan before reapplying.
